selection_criteria: The 80 most recently published GitHub-reviewed advisories for the pip ecosystem as of 2026-08-07, capped at 2 per source repository and 1 per fixing commit, restricted to those carrying a CWE and a fixing-commit reference into their own repository whose parent is not a merge, whose fix diff is under 400 KB, and which touch reviewable Python source outside tests and docs. Ground-truth spans are the lines the fix removed, excluding spans that are entirely imports, version bumps or comments. Two fixing commits were then excluded by hand as bulk refactors whose spans mark remediation plumbing rather than the defect; the reasons are in benchmark/corpus/labelled-excluded.txt. NOT filtered by CWE: classes no 3a detector can emit are retained and reported as a stratum. Newest-first sampling makes the set post-cutoff for any model evaluated later.

findings.title: Namespace prefix scoping no longer segment-boundary safe

evidence.why: ns_condition now uses plain LIKE on unescaped, unanchored text (`prefix%`), so a namespace_prefix of `foo` matches sibling namespaces like `foobar`, causing cross-tenant data disclosure in search results.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: SQLite namespace_prefix search no longer segment/case aware, uses raw LIKE

evidence.why: Replaces GLOB-based case-sensitive, segment-anchored, escaped matching with LIKE, which is case-insensitive for ASCII and unescaped, so `foo` matches `FOO`/`foobar` and labels with `%`/`_` are misinterpreted, breaking namespace isolation guarantees.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: list_namespaces prefix/suffix matching unescaped and unanchored on SQLite

evidence.why: cond.path is joined into a LIKE pattern without escaping `%`/`_` or anchoring at segment boundaries, so namespace prefix/suffix filters can match unintended sibling or substring namespaces, leaking entries across logical namespace boundaries.

AIOHTTP: HTTP request smuggling via WebSocket upgrade

findings.title: Upgrade now takes effect before request body is read

evidence.why: The diff removes the deferred-upgrade logic (RFC 9110 §7.8-15) and sets self._upgraded immediately when the upgrade header is seen, skipping payload creation for Content-Length/chunked bodies on upgrade requests; a rejected/declined upgrade's body is left unread in the stream and will be misinterpreted as the start of the next (upgraded or pipelined) protocol data, enabling request smuggling between a declined upgrade and the following pipelined request.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: C parser also switches to upgraded before body fully consumed

evidence.why: The pending-upgrade deferral removed here means _upgraded is set as soon as the upgrade header is parsed rather than after the body is fully read via HPE_PAUSED_UPGRADE handling, so any request/response body bytes present on an upgrade request can be treated as post-upgrade protocol data, causing desynchronization between what the application handler reads and what is actually on the wire (smuggling risk).

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

advisory.summary: AIOHTTP: HTTP request smuggling via WebSocket upgrade

findings.title: Client WebSocketReader no longer pins compress to negotiated value

evidence.why: The call now omits compress=bool(compress), relying on the reader's compress=True default, so the client will decompress and accept RSV1 frames from a server even though permessage-deflate was never negotiated on this connection.
